adjudication:
I wrote /workspace/minlp-notes/paper-open-minlplib/development/reviews/round1/adjudication.md. It turns the ten round-1 reviews into one deduplicated change list of 97 items, grouped by editor (G1–G7), plus 18 rejections with reasons. I edited no paper source, committed nothing and ran no scientific script. The only checks were reads of stored data and logs and a few small exact computations in /tmp.

**Counts per group and severity:**

| Group | Items | Blocker | Major | Minor | Accept | Accept-modified |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| G1 front | 16 | 1 | 5 | 10 | 9 | 7 |
| G2 results and split | 15 | 0 | 7 | 8 | 10 | 5 |
| G3 other, points, audit | 13 | 0 | 5 | 8 | 9 | 4 |
| G4 solvers and end | 9 | 1 | 5 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| G5 supplement certificates I | 14 | 0 | 5 | 9 | 13 | 1 |
| G6 supplement certificates II | 12 | 0 | 4 | 8 | 11 | 1 |
| G7 supplement other, generators, bib, artifact | 18 | 2 | 9 | 7 | 13 | 5 |
| **Total** | **97** | **4** | **40** | **53** | **69** | **28** |

The four blockers:
- **G1-01:** the AI-use disclosure and the definition of "separately written" in §2.6.
- **G4-01:** the AI-use statement in the declarations.
- **G7-01 and G7-02:** the clipped Table 2 and Table S42.

**What the file contains:**
- **Working rules and order of work:** generators and `numbers.json` belong to G7, and the figure script to G2. Certificate boxes move to the supplement before the main text drops them, and the claim register is rebuilt last.
- **The seven lead-author decisions** (LD-1 to LD-7), each mapped to its items.
- **Page budgets:** Sections 1–11 go from 45.8 to 38.0 pages (G1 9.0, G2 10.0, G3 11.5, G4 7.5). The supplement goes from 130 to 100 pages (G5 32, G6 29, G7 39).
- **A coverage index** that maps every numbered review item to an item id or a rejection.

**Facts I checked while adjudicating:**
- **Second implementations:** the records show they came from separate AI-agent sessions. Those sessions could read the first code and sometimes did. One OSIL reader is shared across several families. The records do not say which model ran each session. The §2.6 text is worded to claim no more independence than that; the bracketed family lists still have to be confirmed against the verification reports.
- **Three unsafe upper ends in the S4 second-proof table:** I confirmed them exactly from the JSON logs. They change to -983842.2577881223, 0.0079302187993 and -1.12968744117115.
- **Campaign:** only BARON's runs on camshape100 and camshape200 end within 10^-6. Of the 109 finite dual bounds, 79 are same-model bounds with a globality guarantee and no tightened bounds; the other 30 are 6 BARON values without a guarantee, 6 SCIP bounds on tightened models and 18 KAN comparisons. The 79 is my one-off count from `results.csv` and still has to be added to the generator with a check (G7-06).
- **topopt replay:** it has no stored basis, so §10's claim that it "replays exactly" is wrong.
- **Prior status:** camshape200 was "listed solve" and camshape800 "none", although both have listings on rounded copies. Making both "related model" changes the partition from 7/8/16 to 7/9/15.
- **Table S42:** the dropped optcdeg2 row is register entry `reported-39`, so the register goes from 66 to 65 entries.
- **Claim builder:** `build_claims.py` still tests the obsolete `\evid{P}`/`\evid{S}` macros, so a rebuild as is would label every entry "computed".

**Main rejections:** a separate audit paper; a new solver experiment for §9; restructuring the archive directories; moving Appendices A and B to the supplement; a main-text glossary; promoting Figure S4; filling the DOI, licence and author placeholders (LD-1(b)); and cutting the headline to 19 bounds. The headline stays at 22 because the rocket proofs and the GAMS/OSIL comparison have now been rerun.

**Corrections to reviewer details:**
- The araya2025 BibTeX entry uses issue 3, not 2.
- The proposed "eleven by less than the gap tolerance" becomes "eleven proved margins below 10^-6".
- The reviewer's powerflow reading-(c) proof does not cover powerflow0030p; that instance needs its own exact check or the label "(computed)".

**Still open:**
- The AI wording in §2.6 and in the declarations is marked [authors to confirm]. The authors also need to say which proofs or codes they read themselves.
- Filing the SCIP issue is an action for the authors, not a text change.
